import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import CaggMigratePermissions from "../../../../partials/_caggs-migrate-permissions.mdx";

In {C.TIMESCALE_DB} v2.7 and later, {C.CAGG}s use a new format that
improves performance and makes them compatible with more SQL queries. {C.CAGG_CAP}s
created in older versions of {C.TIMESCALE_DB}, or created in a new version
with the option `timescaledb.finalized` set to `false`, use the old format.

To migrate a {C.CAGG} from the old format to the new format, you can
use this procedure. It automatically copies over your data and policies. You can
continue to use the {C.CAGG} while the migration is happening.

Connect to your database and run:

```sql
CALL cagg_migrate('<CONTINUOUS_AGGREGATE_NAME>');
```

<Callout variant="warning">
There are known issues with `cagg_migrate()` in version 2.8.0.
Upgrade to version 2.8.1 or later before using it.
</Callout>

## Configure {C.CAGG} migration

The migration procedure provides two boolean configuration parameters,
`override` and `drop_old`. By default, the name of your new {C.CAGG}
is the name of your old {C.CAGG}, with the suffix `_new`.

Set `override` to true to rename your new {C.CAGG} with the
original name. The old {C.CAGG} is renamed with the suffix `_old`.

To both rename and drop the old {C.CAGG} entirely, set both
parameters to true. Note that `drop_old` must be used together with
`override`.

## Check on {C.CAGG} migration status

To check the progress of the {C.CAGG} migration, query the migration
planning table:

```sql
SELECT * FROM _timescaledb_catalog.continuous_agg_migrate_plan_step;
```
